cards.question: Why do we go to Mass every Sunday?
cards.answer: Jesus rose from the dead on a Sunday, so Sunday is the Lord's special day. We go to Mass to thank God together as his family. The Church asks every Catholic to come each Sunday and on holy days.

cards.question: What is the Mass?
cards.answer: The Mass is the greatest prayer of the Church. We remember Jesus' Last Supper and his gift of himself on the cross, and it becomes present for us today. Jesus is with us in a very special way.

cards.question: What are the two big parts of the Mass?
cards.answer: First comes the Liturgy of the Word, when we listen to God in the Bible. Then comes the Liturgy of the Eucharist, when the bread and wine become Jesus. Together they make one big prayer.

cards.answer: We begin Mass in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. It reminds us that we belong to God. The priest then greets us: “The Lord be with you.”

cards.answer: In the readings God himself speaks to us. We usually hear a reading from the Old Testament, a psalm, a letter from the apostles and the Gospel. Listening carefully helps us know God better.

cards.answer: Jesus used bread and wine at the Last Supper, so the Church always uses them for Mass. Families carry the gifts to the altar. We can offer our own hearts to God too.

cards.question: What happens to the bread and wine?
cards.answer: When the priest says Jesus' own words, the bread and wine become Jesus' Body and Blood. They still look and taste like bread and wine, but they are really Jesus. The Church calls this change transubstantiation.

cards.answer: Yes! Jesus is truly present, his Body and Blood, soul and divinity, in the Eucharist. Even a small piece of the Host is the whole Jesus. That is why we treat the Eucharist with great love.

cards.answer: Children usually receive First Communion around age 7, after learning about Jesus and going to their first Confession. cards.answer: The priest wears special clothes called vestments. Their colours tell us the season: green for Ordinary Time, purple for Advent and Lent, white or gold for Christmas and Easter, and red for the Holy Spirit and martyrs. Look at the colour each week!

cards.answer: We come a little early, dress nicely and stay quiet so everyone can pray. We bless ourselves with holy water, genuflect toward the tabernacle, sing and answer the prayers. Being respectful shows our love for Jesus.

cards.question: What is a sacrament?
cards.answer: A sacrament is a holy sign that Jesus gave to his Church. Through it God's grace, his life and love, really comes to us. Each sacrament uses things we can see, like water, oil or bread, together with special words.

cards.answer: Baptism is the first sacrament. It washes away original sin and all sins, and makes us children of God. We become members of the Church and receive the Holy Spirit.

cards.answer: The priest or deacon pours water on the head three times, or the person goes into the water. He says, “I baptise you in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.” We also receive a white garment and a candle.

cards.question: The Ten Commandments
cards.answer:
1. I am the Lord your God:
you shall not have strange gods before me
2. You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain.
3. Remember to keep holy the Sabbath day.
4. Honour your father and your mother.
5. You shall not kill.
6. You shall not commit adultery.
7. You shall not steal.
8. You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.
9. You shall not covet your neighbor’s wife.
10. You shall not covet your neighbor’s goods.

cards.question: The Confiteor (I Confess)
cards.answer:
I confess to almighty God,
and to you, my brothers and sisters,
that I have sinned through my own fault
strike their breast:
in my thoughts and in my words,
in what I have done,
and in what I have failed to do;
and I ask blessed Mary, ever virgin,
all the angels and saints, and you, my brothers and sisters,
to pray for me to the Lord our God.
May almighty God have mercy on us,
forgive us our sins
and bring us to everlasting life.
Amen.

cards.question: Prayer to the Holy Spirit
cards.answer:
○ Come, O Holy Spirit,
fill the hearts of your faithful
and kindle in them the fire of your love.
● Send forth your Spirit, and they shall be created.
And you will renew the face of the earth.
+ Let us pray:
O God, who have taught the hearts of the faithful by the
light of the Holy Spirit, grant us by that Holy Spirit himself,
to know what is right and ever rejoice in his consolation.
Through Christ our Lord.
◎ Amen

cards.question: Morning Offering
cards.answer:
O Jesus, through the immaculate Heart of Mary,
I offer you my prayers, work,
joys, and sufferings of this day
for all the intentions of your Sacred Heart,
in union with the holy sacrifice of the Mass
throughout the world,
in thanksgiving for your favors,
in reparation for my sins,
for the intentions of all my relatives and friends,
and in particular for the intentions of the Holy Father.
Amen.

cards.question: A Night Prayer
cards.answer:
I adore you, my God,
and I love you with all my heart.
I thank you for having created me,
made me a Christian and kept me this day.
Pardon me the evil I have done,
and if I have done some good,
accept it.
Take care of me while I sleep
and deliver me from all danger.
May your grace be always with me
and with all my loved ones.
Amen.
